name: Palma · Mallorca
tagline: Gothic cathedral, mountain villages and turquoise coves
summary: Mallorca's capital has a beautiful old town and a cathedral on the sea wall. Beyond it are the Tramuntana mountains, stone villages like Deià and Valldemossa, and the cove beaches of the east coast.
seasonNote: July and August are very busy and expensive; many resorts close from November to March but Palma stays open.
arrival: Palma airport is 8 km away; bus A1 reaches the centre in 20 minutes. Ferries run from Barcelona and Valencia.
gettingAround: Walk old Palma. TIB buses and the vintage train to Sóller cover the island; a car is easiest for coves.
foodTip: Ensaïmada pastry for breakfast, pa amb oli with tomato and cured meat, sobrassada sausage and tumbet vegetables.
buyTip: Ensaïmadas in a box for the plane, olive wood, and leather shoes from Inca.
baseArea: The old town (Casco Antiguo) or Santa Catalina for restaurants

items.name: Palma Cathedral (La Seu)
items.summary: A Gothic cathedral on the sea wall with one of the largest rose windows in the world and a canopy by Gaudí.
items.expect: Closed to visits on Sundays except for Mass.
items.tip: Visit mid-morning for the coloured light from the rose window.

items.name: Caló des Moro
items.summary: A tiny cove of turquoise water between pine-covered cliffs, the most photographed beach on the island.
items.expect: Very small, no facilities, a steep rocky path and huge summer crowds.
items.tip: Go at 8 am or late afternoon, or swim at Cala S'Almunia next door.
